newsitem.title: USA: PC stocks hit by IBM downgrade, profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: PC stocks hit by IBM downgrade, profit-taking.

text.p: Shares of personal computer companies slid Thursday following a Salomon Brothers' downgrade in industry giant IBM and some profit-taking by investors taking advantage of a recent rally in technology issues, traders said.
"It's probably a combination of IBM (being downgraded) and just some profit taking," said Patrick Davis, head of over-the-counter trading at Salomon Brothers.
"The computer systems makers are off, and IBM is a part of that," said Greg Nie, senior vice president of technical research at Everen Securities.
IBM shed 1-1/4 to 88-5/8. Dell Computer Corp lost 2-1/16 to 113-9/16, while Gateway 2000 Inc dropped 4 to 70-3/8.

"It's partly IBM, as well as some concern about consumer demand for PCs. There's also been quite a run-up (in share prices) lately, so there's some profit-taking going on," said Vadim Zlotnikov, an analyst with Sanford Bernstein.
Gateway, a direct marketer of personal computers, is among the most vulnerable to concerns about PC demand and its stock was harded hit on Thursday, analysts said.
The American Stock Exchange computer index lost 2.03 points or 0.48 percent to 423.67.

Earlier on Thursday, Salomon Brothers analyst John Jones cut International Business Machines Corp to buy from strong buy. Jones said IBM hit Salomon's target price of $91, on a post-split basis, on May 28.
Despite the downgrade, Jones said he remains positive about IBM's long-term fundamentals and believes the shares could rise to $100 over the next nine months.
